bull.b: Very low leverage reduces refinancing pressure and preserves financial flexibility while InflaRx advances its clinical programs. Although losses remain substantial, the lightly levered balance sheet limits interest-related strain and provides a stronger foundation than a highly indebted biotech.

Broadening development and registration plans across Europe gives InflaRx more ways to pursue a rare, life-threatening autoimmune indication with substantial unmet demand. Continuing Phase 2 planning for izicopan and a Phase 3-ready vilobelimab could strengthen the pipeline’s strategic relevance.

A partner-led Phase 3 program in China provides external development support for a vilobelimab-derived therapy and advances clinical validation without relying solely on InflaRx’s own infrastructure. Positive earlier response data and ongoing execution could expand the platform’s commercial possibilities.

bear.b: The absence of a meaningful and stable revenue base leaves InflaRx dependent on successful clinical development before it can approach operating self-sufficiency. Persistent large losses also make earnings highly dependent on external funding and increase the time required to establish durable profitability.

Persistent negative operating and free cash flow shows that the business is not yet self-funding its research and development activities. Even though TTM burn improved versus 2025, inconsistent free-cash-flow progress means continued capital raises may be needed, creating financing and dilution pressure.

The EMA development reshapes the AAV regulatory and competitive landscape while InflaRx works to define the most efficient route for vilobelimab and izicopan. Reviewing the pathway introduces uncertainty around timing, evidence requirements, and resources needed to reach potential commercialization.
